    AI Overview
    The "Arctic Frost" investigation is a
    Senate Judiciary Committee-led probe into a 2022 FBI inquiry regarding the 2020 election "false electors scheme". Led by Senator Chuck Grassley, the oversight alleges that the FBI and Special Counsel Jack Smith improperly targeted hundreds of Republicans, including members of Congress, via surveillance and phone record subpoenas. 
    Key findings and allegations regarding the Arctic Frost investigation include: 
    • Investigation Scope: Opened in April 2022 by the FBI, the investigation was later incorporated into Special Counsel Jack Smith's case against Donald Trump.
    • Targeting of Officials: Oversight revealed the FBI and DOJ obtained records for at least nine Republican members of Congress (eight senators and one House member)
      .
    • Scope of Surveillance: Over 400 Republican-affiliated organizations and individuals were reportedly targeted, according to Senator Chuck Grassley.
    • Allegations of Misconduct: Critics, including Senator Grassley, claim the operation was politically motivated, constituting "lawfare" and a violation of the Fourth Amendment.
    • Key Figures: The inquiry highlights roles played by Special Counsel Jack Smith, FBI Assistant Special Agent in Charge Timothy Thibault, and high-ranking DOJ officials in approving the investigation.
    • Congressional Response: Senator Grassley and Senator Ron Johnson are conducting an investigation into the FBI’s actions, aiming to release records and hold hearings in 2026. 
    Note: The results also mention "Arctic-FROST," a separate, unrelated research project focused on Arctic sustainability based at the University of Northern Iowa.
